correctness.rationale: All labels and graph neighborhoods defined. For zero A_i (B_i), the count of adjacent twos is q-[B_i=2] (respectively p-[A_i=2]). Independent selection of remaining 0/1 labels after choosing the two-support sets yields F_n by four disjoint index classes. A perfect Roman labeling has no side with zero positives for n>=3; totality is equivalent to at least two positives per side. Exact enumeration of all one-positive-side exceptions and their overlap gives T_n=F_n-2E_n+n z^4. A separate case split on p and q proves the weight-six minimum and all n^2(n-1) optimizers for n>=4, with 31 exceptions at n=3. Standalone adjacency-based code exhaustively verifies n=3..6 (597780 assignments); finite verification is supplemental, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Almulhim (Symmetry 15 (2023), 1676, DOI 10.3390/sym15091676) introduces total perfect Roman domination and proves multipartite and cyclic minimum results, but a crown is not complete multipartite and the only cyclic overlap is the scalar n=3 instance. The public published-finding corpus ordinary-perfect-Roman crown statement concerns a strictly weaker property and cannot imply the new full total-perfect-Roman polynomial or its n>=4 optimizer formula. value.rationale: An exact full weight distribution and optimizer classification in the canonical graph perturbation \(\(K_{n,n}\)-M\) distinguish function support structure from a scalar domination bound. Matched-pair deletion raises the previously established complete-bipartite minimum 4 to 6 for every n>=3, while minimum multiplicity grows as n^2(n-1) for n>=4. These are motivated structural enumeration and edge-deletion sensitivity results, not an arbitrary size slice.
